policy.scope: Explicitly reviewed semantic/paraphrase equivalences supplement exact stem/options/accepted-answer matching. This is not topic-level clustering.
policy.equivalence: Same tested relation and compatible reviewed answer; preserve negation, molecule identity, numerical values, clinical target and required figure. No media-dependent question is manually merged here.
policy.counting: Question occurrences remain distinct. Independent recurrence uses source-families.json and at most one exam-family vote; recall/practice members are support only.
policy.excluded: Opposite pKa directions, different named syndromes, essential versus polyunsaturated fatty acids, different inhibition examples, changed numerical problems and incompatible accepted-answer sets are not merged just because words or answers overlap.

groups.label: Vitamin K coenzyme for gamma-carboxylation
groups.reason: Same vitamin-to-gamma-carboxylation relation. The scan spells gamma as y; the answer remains menaquinone.

groups.label: Constitutively expressed lac regulatory gene
groups.reason: Same lac-operon gene identification, with reordered options and unchanged i-gene answer.

groups.label: Vitamin B12 as a methyl-group acceptor
groups.reason: Same methyl-acceptor question; Vit B12 and Vitamin B12 are synonymous. Includes the repeated January page without creating an extra family vote.

groups.label: Lowest melting point among the same four fatty acids
groups.reason: All variants compare palmitic, stearic, arachidonic and eicosapentaenoic acids. Identical comparative target and EPA answer; option order differs.

groups.label: Pantothenic acid active coenzyme
groups.reason: Same vitamin B5-to-coenzyme A identification; distractors vary but the requested active coenzyme and correct answer do not.

groups.label: Cholesterol-rich LDL
groups.reason: Same lipoprotein cholesterol-composition comparison among chylomicron, VLDL, LDL and HDL. Does not merge LDL cardiovascular-risk questions.

groups.label: Topoisomerase relieves replication supercoiling
groups.reason: Same enzyme for DNA supercoil relief during replication; helicase unwinding questions remain separate.

groups.label: Vitamin E as a lipid-soluble membrane antioxidant
groups.reason: Singular/plural membrane wording and distractor changes do not alter the vitamin E antioxidant relation.

groups.label: Cardiolipin lacks sphingosine
groups.reason: Not a component and component of all except express the same negative target. Same four lipid choices and cardiolipin answer.

groups.label: Glutamate pI with pKa 2.3, 4.2 and 9.3
groups.reason: The amino acid, all three numerical pKa values and pI answer 3.25 are identical; only value order and wording change.

groups.label: Carbon monoxide increases hemoglobin oxygen affinity
groups.reason: Same four physiological changes and same CO answer. CO2, pH and temperature alternatives are not merged as distinct questions.

groups.label: Isoenzymes catalyze the same reaction
groups.reason: All ask for the false isoenzyme statement and key different reactions. Same negative target, with a scan typo in not.

groups.label: Alpha and beta glucose are anomers
groups.reason: Same alpha-versus-beta glucose relationship; one source explicitly writes D. Both distinguish the most specific offered relationship, anomers.

groups.label: Heparin as an anticoagulant carbohydrate
groups.reason: Same carbohydrate-to-anticoagulant use relation; the shorter biosynthesis wording and clinical vignette identify heparin. Homopolysaccharide classification is excluded.

groups.label: Hydrogen bonds join complementary DNA strands
groups.reason: Same interstrand bond question; intrachain phosphodiester questions stay separate. The student compilation is support only.

groups.label: Rifamycin inhibition of prokaryotic transcription initiation
groups.reason: Same antibiotic and promoter/RNA-polymerase initiation target, with reordered distractors.

groups.label: Vitamin D does not hydroxylate connective-tissue proteins
groups.reason: Repeated January page with an OCR spelling difference; same negative stem and identical choices. One source family only.

groups.label: Liver and kidney activate vitamin D
groups.reason: Same organ-pair activation target and liver/kidney answer, including minor OCR truncation.

groups.label: Lower pKa means stronger acid
groups.reason: Same direction of pKa change and acid-strength answer. The opposite higher-pKa prompt is deliberately excluded.

groups.label: Inulin measurement of glomerular filtration
groups.reason: Same carbohydrate used to measure GFR; differing distractors do not change inulin as the requested marker.

groups.label: Arachidonic acid is the exception to 18-carbon fatty acids
groups.reason: Same negative carbon-count target and same four fatty-acid alternatives; number 18 is preserved.

groups.label: Collagen defect in Ehlers–Danlos syndrome
groups.reason: Same named disorder and defective-protein identification; Marfan/fibrillin items are deliberately excluded.

groups.label: Noncompetitive inhibition lowers Vmax with unchanged Km
groups.reason: Same noncompetitive inhibition kinetic effects. Max is an OCR shortening of Vmax. Competitive-inhibition changes remain a separate relation.

groups.label: RNA caps are characteristic of eukaryotic mRNA
groups.reason: Same cap-specificity statement and answer. Different incorrect 3-prime RNA distractors do not change the tested relation.

groups.label: Primase synthesizes RNA primers
groups.reason: Same enzyme-to-RNA-primer synthesis question, including reordered polymerase alternatives.

groups.label: Repressor prevents lac structural-gene transcription
groups.reason: Same lac z/y/a structural genes and repressor action. Gene order and capitalization differ.

groups.label: Hydrophobic interactions dominate protein tertiary folding

groups.label: Vitamin C supports collagen production and maintenance

groups.label: Fibrillin defect in Marfan syndrome

groups.label: Folate deficiency causes megaloblastic anemia

groups.label: Gamma-carboxylation is not biotin-dependent

groups.label: Glycosphingolipids contain ceramide plus sugar

groups.label: Biuret is the qualitative protein test

groups.label: Chromatographic mobile phase may be liquid or gas

groups.label: Starch is the insoluble carbohydrate among these choices
groups.reason: Soluble except and insoluble express the same negative target. Same fructose/sucrose/glucose/starch comparison; no change in solution context.

groups.label: Dihydroxyacetone is achiral
groups.reason: Lack of a chiral carbon and inability to form D/L stereoisomers ask the same chirality relation for dihydroxyacetone; other carbohydrate-isomer classifications stay separate.

groups.label: Humans cannot digest cellulose
groups.reason: Same lack of human enzymatic digestion of cellulose; distractor carbohydrates differ but the digestive capability tested is identical.

groups.label: Linoleic acid must be supplied in the diet
groups.reason: Essential and cannot synthesize/must obtain from diet ask the same linoleic-acid relation. Polyunsaturated classification and linolenic-acid variants are excluded.

groups.label: Operator is the repressor-binding sequence

groups.label: Catalytic efficiency is kcat over Km
groups.reason: Same catalytic-efficiency parameter, including comparison of two enzymes; kcat/Km is preserved.

groups.label: Platelet-activating factor contains an ether linkage
groups.reason: Same identification of an ether-containing lipid, with identical answer and equivalent lipid distractors.

groups.label: Pyridoxine supports transamination
groups.reason: Same vitamin-to-amino-acid transamination relation; cofactor phrasing does not alter the answer.

groups.label: Thiamine deficiency causes beriberi
groups.reason: Thiamine and vitamin B1 are equivalent; same deficiency-disease target and beriberi answer.

groups.label: Glucose is the glycogen precursor
groups.reason: Same precursor monosaccharide and animal glycogen context; same four choices.

groups.label: Pentose-phosphate pathway produces NADPH
groups.reason: Phosphogluconate pathway and HMP shunt denote the same pathway. Same reducing-equivalent production target; two occurrences within one source still yield one family vote.

groups.label: Beta sheets are secondary protein structure
groups.reason: Same structural-level classification; Greek beta and spelled-out beta are equivalent. Dated quiz variants share one family.

groups.label: Collagen is rich in glycine and proline
groups.reason: Same requested pair of abundant collagen amino acids, with equivalent options.

groups.label: Niacin deficiency causes pellagra
groups.reason: Same vitamin-deficiency disease, unchanged answer and alternatives.

groups.label: Linolenic acid must be supplied in the diet
groups.reason: Same essential-fatty-acid relation with linolenic acid as the offered answer. Kept separate from linoleic-acid variants because the selected molecule changes.

groups.label: Phosphodiester bonds connect adjacent nucleotides
groups.reason: Same within-strand nucleotide linkage; complementary-strand hydrogen bonding is excluded. Both source documents are supporting compilations.

groups.label: Millon test identifies tyrosine
groups.reason: Same reagent-to-amino-acid identification; distractor amino acids differ without changing the target.

groups.label: DNA ligase joins DNA ends
groups.reason: Same DNA-end joining/nick-sealing enzyme relation, including Okazaki-fragment joining. Student questions provide supporting evidence only.

groups.label: Rifampicin inhibits bacterial RNA polymerase
groups.reason: Same antibiotic inhibition of prokaryotic DNA-dependent RNA polymerase; one wording describes initiation at the promoter. Rifamycin-class wording is retained in its own group rather than silently equated to a specific member.

groups.label: Absorbed dietary fat circulates in chylomicrons
groups.reason: Same transport form after dietary-fat absorption; dotted blanks, option order and an HDL scan typo do not change the chylomicron target.

groups.label: Tryptophan and phenylalanine operons are anabolic
groups.reason: Same anabolic-operon question; both variants accept Trp and Phe. Abbreviated gene-set names do not alter the accepted answer set.

groups.label: Sigma factor recognizes transcription initiation sites

groups.label: HDL is synthesized in liver and intestine
groups.reason: Same HDL origin question and organ-pair answer; only dotted blanks and option order differ.

groups.label: Ciprofloxacin inhibits DNA gyrase
groups.reason: Same drug-to-enzyme target, with shortened prompt and minor topoisomerase/polymerase distractor spelling differences.

groups.label: Sickle cell hemoglobin has an amino-acid substitution
groups.reason: Same molecular basis of sickle cell disease; distractor changes do not alter the single-amino-acid substitution target.

groups.label: Amylopectin has alpha-1,4 and alpha-1,6 linkages

groups.label: Polar residues lie on the aqueous protein surface
groups.reason: Same aqueous-environment protein localization question and four alternatives; punctuation differs.

groups.reason: Same false statement about Km versus substrate affinity. Retains the negative target; variations in the true distractors do not change the accepted false relation.

groups.label: Telomerase has reverse-transcriptase activity
groups.reason: Same enzyme activity question and telomerase answer. An incorrect polymerase II/beta option differs; the same-source family still supplies one vote.

groups.label: VLDL is pre-beta lipoprotein
groups.reason: Same alternative lipoprotein name; Greek beta and the scanned B spelling refer to the same electrophoretic designation.
